stem_book: Fig. shows the projectile motion (projected with speed u at angle α, max height H, range R, striking the ground at angle θ with speed v) in the absence of air resistance. If air resistance is taken into account, then (one or more correct): (a) time taken by projectile during upward motion is lesser than time taken during downward motion (b) θ > α (c) the value of height attained and of range of projectile decreases (d) v < u
key: abcd all four printed options — (a) time taken by projectile during upward motion is lesser than time taken during downward motion; (b) θ > α; (c) the value of height attained and of range of projectile decreases; (d) v < u
work: drag adds to g going up (a_up > g) and subtracts coming down (a_down < g) ⇒ t_up < t_down; H, R fall; horizontal speed keeps dropping ⇒ steeper landing θ > α; energy lost ⇒ v < u ⇒ a, b, c, d
